scope: Crash recovery of SendPost continuations in the existing single-Map ownership domain. No publisher quest rules or rewards are invented.
implemented: Migration 042 adds dbo.TQuestPostOperation. Reservation attachments, completed quest counter and a pending continuation commit in the same SQL transaction. Each issuance has a GUID frozen with its rolled attachments in the local journal before SQL. Replaying that same identity, even for uncapped mail or after an ambiguous commit, does not reserve more attachments. Reusing it with a different payload fails.

Sibling mail requests already queued for the character are captured together. Completed character state, pending nested mail requests and continuation receipts share a version-2 journal record. Incremental item operations are included in that SAME record and applied before the full inventory snapshot; no separate item-publication gap remains for these mail checkpoints. Cabinet/direct operation order is preserved.

The real snapshot callback applies every character/pet/companion stage, reserves nested mail by its frozen identity, then acknowledges the parent continuation as its last stage. On restart, pending journal records finish before character loading. SQL pending continuations then execute at the main's CS_CONREADY admission boundary, before world placement.

Child mission, item, skill and repeatable craft results recover without another parent/sibling/nested mail or another payout in the tested graph. Child replies are buffered. SQL/file failures close the session, suppress those replies and prevent unpublished in-memory state from leaking through direct, logout or map-leave quest execution. Unrelated characters' pending item work is retained.

An intent pins the quest-chart hash, event target/position/map/channel and ancestor path. A changed chart, malformed/unknown intent, unavailable required outbox or unseeded allocator denies recovery. Cyclic asynchronous mail ancestors cannot recurse indefinitely. Previously written version-1 records remain readable; new version-2 records are deliberately rejected by an older version-1-only executable.

history_review.reason: Reservation/progress previously committed before in-memory children, leaving no durable record when a process died between them. A plain outbox acknowledgement before saving the child result would also lose actions; acknowledgement after an independent item flush could pay them twice. The new WAL record joins the child result, direct operations, nested intents and receipt; the acknowledgement is last after replayable native SQL stages. Initial/sibling intents are also frozen before the first reservation.
history_review.retained: Native chart CountMax, byte rollover, item/text encoding, class/skill/reward prevalidation, local main ownership and official-baseline priorities. No content, balance, mail caps or Gameforge conquest/soul rules were changed.

remaining: Continuations that invoke Teleport, Switch, SpawnMon, DieMon, DropItem or Regen have external/world effects without a durable replay contract. They are explicitly blocked and left pending, rather than acknowledged or blindly replayed. Supporting these graphs needs a separate world-effect protocol; the audited 35 inherited SendPost templates currently have no TT_EXECQUEST children.
Cross-Map owner fencing/routing is still incomplete. This implementation does not claim coordination or exactly-once gameplay across independently writing Map servers.

Real-client startup/admission, mailed-reward collection, complete logout/restart and pinned Gameforge compatibility remain acceptance gates. The actual MapWorker process has not been restarted with this build.
RT_SOUL mission rewards and TT_WARREGION event rules still lack compatible reference evidence. No EXP/soul substitute or conquest trigger was guessed.

Initial incoming gameplay events have no general durable identity before their checkpoint is published. Storage durability still depends on the configured filesystem honoring Flush/WriteThrough; loss of the journal volume or power failure is not certified.
